extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / wartime public (and editors/war-correspondents)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and compiling timely wartime news items for a newspaper/homepage, including battlefield dispatches, official communiqués, diplomatic notes, naval/air actions, and domestic wartime developments. Emphasizes sourcing, datelines, casualty/equipment figures, context, and bite-sized subheads for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and wire-service credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear dateline and wire-service attribution (e.g., "Moscow, Oct. 15—(AP)—", "London, Oct. 15—(AP)—") for each dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datelines signal location and timeliness; wire-credit shows the reporting source. Use them prominently to orient readers to where and when the report originated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute claims to specific sources (official communiqués, newspapers, agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting military movements or political statements, explicitly say who made the claim (e.g., "the communique said", "the army newspaper Red Star said", "the Tass agency circulated").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the issuing body (communique, army newspaper, government office, radio broadcast) and, when relevant, include wording or quotations. This preserves transparency and allows readers to weigh source reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report opposing or contradictory claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Present both sides' statements when they differ (e.g., Soviet communiqués vs. German broadcasts; Berlin radio denials vs. Stockholm reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place competing claims side-by-side and indicate conflicts or denials; flag when information is from enemy propaganda outlets or unverified enemy broadcasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include casualty, equipment and unit figures with qualifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish numbers of killed/wounded/captured and materiel losses (e.g., "disabling nineteen German tanks and killing approximately two companies of enemy infantry", "about 400 of the enemy").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact figures when available but include qualifiers such as "reported", "approximately", or the source name. Avoid presenting unverified counts as definitive; indicate when figures come from official press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide strategic and historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Situate current events within broader context (e.g., comparisons to "a year ago", references to prior battles like Kharkov or earlier phases of the Stalingrad fighting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain significance, prior outcomes, logistical factors (e.g., winter readiness), and likely implications so readers understand why an item matters beyond the immediate facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use named-person profiles and human-interest details
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short profiles or humanizing details about key figures and civilians (e.g., "36-Year-Old General Is Hero Of Stalingrad", anecdotes about wounded civilians or pilots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles and concrete human examples break up operational reporting and help readers connect emotionally; include ranks, roles, notable deeds, and quotes where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark unverified or propaganda-suspect information clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag reports that may be propaganda or unconfirmed (phrases in the text: "claimed", "was reported", "broadcasts said", "it was said").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cautious language, attribute to source, and avoid definitive framing until corroborated. Note when a report is known only through broadcasts or secondary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix operational, diplomatic, economic, and domestic wartime coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A wartime news compilation includes battlefield dispatches, diplomatic notes (e.g., Molotov's note proposing trials), naval/air actions, economic reports (wheat and rye yields, insurance rates), and domestic legal/crime items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance front-line military news with policy/diplomatic developments and home-front stories to reflect the multifaceted impact of war on readers' lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concise headlines and subheads to structure copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Break long dispatches into labeled sections and use bold or short subheads (e.g., "Red Army Admits Minor Penetration", "Soviet Statement Mentions Names").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subheads guide skimming readers on a homepage; they should summarize the key fact or angle of the paragraph that follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ multiple corroborating wire services and dispatches
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate and cross-reference reports from AP, Reuters, DNB, Tass, London papers, Stockholm dispatches, CBS pickups, etc., to build a fuller picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite different agencies and correspondents; when multiple sources corroborate an event, say so to increase confidence. Where reports conflict, present both attributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localize reports with place names and sector details
rubrics_metrics.description: Give precise geographic markers—front names, cities, sectors, distances (e.g., "Bryansk front, about 210 miles southwest of Moscow", "Volga on a two-mile front", "Mozdok area of the central Caucasus").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific place names and distances help readers assess scale and proximity. Use widely recognized locational references and link them to larger theaters or maps where possible.
